# Notes & lists — Android integration
## Setup and scope
- The existing Collections/home section is now **Notes & lists**. Login and the global start screen are unchanged. Existing Notes detail/create routes open the same typed workspace; the legacy untyped editors are no longer routed from the app. - Uses the existing configured HTTPS server, encrypted bearer-token session, login roles, Material 3 themes and Android string/plural resources. No credentials, bot configuration, new dependencies or data import is required. - The shared Retrofit provider normalizes the configured URL to its HTTPS origin; full `/api/...` paths are not prefixed twice. Authenticated 401 responses invalidate the rejected session using the existing username/password reauthentication flow. Requests are not automatically replayed and have a 30-second call timeout. - Deploy the backend folder-type/item-field migrations first. Existing records are read in place. A missing legacy folder type is displayed as Diary without rewriting any item. - `Writer` and `Admin` can edit; Reader, unknown and missing roles are read-only. Older sessions without stored role metadata require a fresh password login to expose writes. - **Notes data is shared among authenticated accounts.** The current backend has no per-user Notes ownership filter and does not enforce the Writer/Admin UI policy. Client controls are not server authorization or privacy guarantees. - Android minimum API 24, compile/target API 37. There is no iOS target in this repository. No Solarized theme exists; the workspace follows the existing light/dark theme.
## Connected behavior
- Folder navigator contains folders only, including nested folders, independent type icons, direct counts, indentation and selected state. It never contains item titles or completion controls. - The main list uses only `selectedFolder.notes`, in the server's returned order. Child and parent notes are not combined. All returned items remain available in a lazy list. - Phones use folder → direct items → editor navigation. At 840 dp and wider, folder-only navigation, the direct-item list and editor remain separate panes. The folder pane can be hidden/restored. - Root and child folder creation default independently to Diary. Folder name/type/position can be configured; mutation responses never replace cached subtrees because their children/notes are empty. Tree refresh selects the created/edited folder. - Buy lists show title/Purchased; task lists show title, description, optional end date/Done; Diary shows title, multiline content, whole-note style controls and preview. Position and destination folder are common controls. - Diary style is not HTML or rich-text spans. Controls preserve all five style properties and offer 14/16/18/20/24 font sizes; existing other font sizes are retained unless changed. - Numeric IDs identify folders/items. Partial PUT payloads contain changed fields only. Immediate list completion writes contain **only** `completed`, including explicit false. Unchanged hidden content, style, description, end date and completion are omitted, not reset. - End dates remain ISO calendar strings and never pass through UTC. Clearing sends `endDate: ""`, not null. Dates may be in the past; no date-ordering restriction is added. - Folder type changes do not write notes or children. Moving an item selects its destination and the saved item after refresh. Drafts retain all fields when destination type changes. - Save/delete operations are serialized. Failed writes retain input and do not optimistically toggle or delete rows. Confirmed saves refetch the tree and reselect the saved item; failed refreshes show **saved, refresh failed** and an independent refresh retry. - Uncertain writes are not replayed. A successful reconciliation and explicit user review are required before new writes. A malformed body after confirmed HTTP success is treated as saved; the duplicate-create draft is closed and the tree is reconciled. - Item deletion requires confirmation, closes the editor on success and refetches the selected folder. Cancel sends no mutation. Dirty navigation requires explicit discard; canceling folder creation preserves the previous selected folder. - Refresh on screen return/resume and pull-to-refresh; old responses are generation-guarded. Session/account/API changes cancel work and clear client selections, drafts and cached tree. No disk Notes cache or offline queue exists.
## Reordering folders and notes (restored 10 November 2026)
- Writer/Admin users can drag the reorder handle on folder cards and on direct notes/items in every folder type: Diary, Buy list and Tasks list. Dragging only previews the order; position changes are submitted once the handle is released. - Tap the same handle for **Move up** / **Move down**. Equivalent screen-reader custom actions are available, and actions at the first/last boundary are disabled. Readers have no reorder controls. A single sibling has no unnecessary handle. - Root folders reorder among roots. Nested folders reorder only among siblings under the same parent. A moved folder keeps all children and notes attached; dragging does not reparent folders or mix notes into the folder navigator. - Notes reorder within the selected folder's direct-item list, not across folders. Existing destination-folder editing remains the way to move an item elsewhere. - Close the editor before reordering, including on tablets. Handles are disabled while an editor is open, during loading/saving, when data is stale, or while an uncertain write still requires review. Unsaved drafts are never discarded by a reorder operation. - Ordered siblings receive consecutive zero-based positions. Only records whose position must change are written. Each PUT body is exactly `{"position": n}`: no name, type, parent/folder, completion, date, content, description or style is sent. Folder mutation responses never replace cached subtrees. - The existing API has no atomic bulk reorder operation. Updates run serially and stop at the first failure. The app always refreshes afterward; it reports an incomplete reorder rather than claiming success if some writes failed. A timeout requires reconciliation/review and is never automatically replayed. A failed refresh retains explicitly stale server data, not a successful-looking preview. - Reordering uses the already-installed reorderable library and the existing Notes endpoints; it does not change the separate UUID/project/cost work-Tasks section.
Regression coverage: `NotesReorderingTest` checks subtree preservation, scope/role guards, position-only bodies, all item types, serialization, duplicate submissions, partial failures, uncertain outcomes and account changes. `NotesReorderingScreenTest` adds real folder/note drag gestures, nested move menus and read-only/editor guards.
### Reordering validation results
- Debug build, instrumentation APK build and lint passed using `gradlew.bat :app:testDebugUnitTest :app:assembleDebug :app:assembleDebugAndroidTest :app:lintDebug --console=plain`. Lint remains at **0 errors, 38 warnings and 2 hints**; no new warning remains. - **77 JVM tests passed**, including **11 new reordering tests**. Existing Notes, work-Tasks, Fuel and JWT regression suites also passed. - **9/9 Notes screen tests passed on each API 35 emulator profile:** small phone (720×1280 px at 320 dpi, 360×640 dp) and wide tablet-size override (1920×1200 px at 240 dpi, 1280×800 dp). Both runs include the five existing Notes cases and four reordering cases. The wide-only pane checks actually ran on the tablet. - The first instrumentation attempt terminated before test results; emulator crash logs also contained Bluetooth-service failures. After the final build, idle Gradle daemons were stopped and emulator Bluetooth was temporarily disabled; both complete runs passed. Display overrides and the previous Bluetooth setting were restored. The attached physical device was not used. - Evidence: `app/build/notes-reordering-final-build.txt`, `app/build/notes-reordering-small-phone.txt`, `app/build/notes-reordering-tablet.txt`, and the usual JVM/lint reports. These are synthetic local fixtures, not staging persistence or physical-device accessibility sign-off. Verify server persistence/reopen and concurrent ordering against disposable shared staging records before release.
## Folder deletion policy
Only **empty leaf folders** are eligible. Nonempty folders or folders with children display an explanation and send no DELETE. Confirmation is explicit; a fresh tree is checked again immediately before an empty-folder DELETE. There is no recursive client deletion sequence and no folder-to-root move control.
The fresh check is not an atomic backend guarantee: another client could add a note/child between that check and DELETE. Safe nonempty/recursive deletion, ownership and stronger authorization/concurrency require separate backend/product agreement. The app does not promise those guarantees.
## Implementation map
- `data/model/NotesWorkspace.kt`: typed tree/item/style models, numeric IDs, offset-aware timestamps, date-only drafts, validation and partial-write builders. - `data/repository/NotesRepository.kt`: exact endpoint/status handling, full item decoding, tree read source, JSON `error` display with bounded plain-text rendering and non-JSON fallbacks. A Notes 400/404 is not assumed to be a field error/already-deleted success. - `data/remote/RetrofitProvider.kt`: existing shared authentication/network integration, HTTPS-origin normalization and no automatic write replay. - `ui/viewmodels/NotesViewModel.kt`: session-scoped, testable controller with preservation-safe drafts, role gating, mutation serialization, stale/error/uncertain state and confirmation targets. - `ui/screens/NotesScreen.kt`: adaptive folder-only workspace, typed native editors and previews, accessible text status, discard/delete confirmations and refresh. - `res/values/notes.xml`: default-English feature strings/plurals, matching the app's current localization convention. Additional language translations are not included.
Notes task lists are unrelated to the work/billing Tasks section: they do not use UUID/project/cost/sentOn updates. Diary items use the Notes API, not `/api/diary`. No Telegram, reminder, notification, background polling or push-registration code is added.
## Initial Notes rollout verification (historical)
Commands executed:
- `gradlew.bat :app:testDebugUnitTest :app:assembleDebug :app:assembleDebugAndroidTest :app:lintDebug --console=plain` - `gradlew.bat :app:testDebugUnitTest :app:assembleDebugAndroidTest --console=plain` after extending the regression cases. - Final verification used the first command with `--no-daemon`, after closing the dedicated emulator; exit code 0, `BUILD SUCCESSFUL`. See `app/build/notes-final-build.log`.
Build and lint passed (zero lint errors; 38 warnings and 2 hints remain). **41 JVM tests passed**, including 24 new Notes tests:
- `NotesContractTest` (10): exact lowercase types, numeric IDs, migration/style defaults, direct tree groups/order, hidden-field omission, explicit false/zero/empty-date, whole-style preservation, root/child defaults, validation, time zones, actual Retrofit paths/statuses, JSON/plain-text failures and malformed confirmed responses. - `NotesControllerTest` (14): nested selection, independent types, root/child create and refresh/reselection, discard protection, field-preserving type changes/moves, completion-only writes, clear-date writes, Reader gating, duplicate prevention, saved-but-refresh-failed, uncertain/rejected draft retention, deletion confirmation/cancel and nonempty preflight, stale response/session separation, validation and 401 without loops. - Existing Fuel/JWT regression tests also pass.
UI suite: `NotesScreenTest` contains five cases for folder-only nesting/read-only controls, Buy completion and discard, task date clearing, large-text dark Diary preview, and wide-pane hide/restore/selection. It uses fake in-memory data, not a real account. The tablet-specific branch must be run at a wide size; a phone-only run is not tablet validation.
Completed on the dedicated Android 15/API 35 emulator:
| Configuration | Result | | --- | --- | | Small phone, 720×1280 px at 320 dpi (360×640 dp), America/Los_Angeles | **13/13 passed**: Auth (5), Fuel (3), Notes (5). The tablet-only case returns early on a phone. | | Wide/tablet, 1920×1200 px at 240 dpi (1280×800 dp) | **5/5 Notes passed**, including actual folder-pane hide/restore and folder-switch/editor assertions. | | Small-phone task date clearing, Asia/Tokyo | **1/1 passed**, again asserting the empty-string payload and preserved description. | | Large text / dark appearance | Diary preview uses 1.8× text and dark theme in both Notes suite sizes; all assertions passed. |
The initial snapshot-restored emulator run stalled/reported a process crash; logs also showed background ANR/memory-pressure activity. After a cold boot with 3072 MiB and stopping idle Gradle work, all runs above passed. No production-device tests or data mutations were performed in these Notes validation runs. Display size/density and time-zone settings were restored before closing the emulator.
Reports/artifacts:
- `app/build/reports/tests/testDebugUnitTest/index.html` - `app/build/reports/lint-results-debug.html` - `app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk` - `app/build/outputs/apk/androidTest/debug/app-debug-androidTest.apk` - `app/build/notes-*-validation.txt` for direct emulator runs. - `docs/notes-screenshots/phone/01-folders-only.png` through `04-diary-preview-large-dark.png`. - `docs/notes-screenshots/tablet/01-folders-only.png` through `05-tablet-folders-items.png`, including the wide split layout.
Use an explicit emulator serial when another physical device is connected. Instrumentation uses fake data, and Auth regression tests clear app-session preferences; never run it against a real user's installed app/data. If the IDE reports unresolved newly generated string resources despite a successful Gradle build, synchronize its Gradle project model.
## Release validation still required
- Dedicated staging HTTPS access and Reader/Writer/Admin accounts were not provided. Validate actual migrated legacy data, server persistence/reopen, real account switching, create/edit/move/delete responses and role policy using disposable shared data only. No real records have been imported, recreated or deleted in this implementation work. - Exercise actual server/network failures, expired sessions, uncertain writes, saved-write/failed-refresh and simultaneous same-field edits from web/mobile. Mocked errors do not establish radio/server reliability. - Complete supported physical-device/API testing (especially API 24/37), TalkBack traversal/announcements, native touch targets, keyboard-open editors, contrast with real themes, translated/long labels and reduced-motion behavior. - Emulator small-phone, wide/tablet, large-text, dark-mode and both-sides-of-UTC results are recorded above. Repeat against staging and supported physical devices before release; fake-data emulator/JVM results do not prove migrated production data or backend policy. - Folder-to-root moves, nonempty/recursive folder deletion, offline queued writes, per-user isolation, new backend authorization and notification scheduling remain out of scope.

# Android Tasks section
Implemented against the Spending Tracker task/project contract dated 9 November 2026. This repository is a native Android application (Jetpack Compose, Hilt, Retrofit/Gson), not the web/backend repository referenced by the handoff. No backend changes or iOS target are included.
## Setup
1. Use the existing Android Studio/Gradle wrapper setup and installed SDKs specified by `app/build.gradle.kts` and `gradle/libs.versions.toml`. 2. Obtain the development/staging/production **HTTPS origin** and a test account from the deployment owner through the normal secure channel. No origin or credentials are embedded in this feature. Use an origin such as `https://your-deployment.example/`, not a device-local `localhost`, and use valid certificates. Do not disable certificate checks. 3. Configure that origin in the existing login screen and sign in normally. Prefer the origin root (without `/api`) for compatibility with the existing Notes/login client. Tasks always addresses `/api/tasks` and `/api/projects` at the origin root, so it never produces `/api/api/...`. 4. Open **Tasks** from the bottom navigation. All authenticated roles use the same actions; task/project data is **shared**, not user-private. **Account** contains the workspace connection, biometric preference, and confirmed sign-out. Bottom navigation is hidden in task details/editors so leaving unsaved edits goes through the normal Back/discard flow.
Bearer tokens reuse the existing session and are now encrypted at rest using a non-exportable Android Keystore AES-GCM key. Existing plaintext stored tokens are migrated on first read. A restored/corrupted encrypted token without its key is invalidated and requires login. Task data is only held in the navigation-entry ViewModel, not persisted as an offline cache. A Tasks 401 clears the session, biometric session flag, Tasks state, and protected navigation stack. There is no refresh-token endpoint or retry loop.
## Walkthrough
1. Open Tasks: **Not sent** is the initial view. Check pending count, pending EUR total, and total task count. Pending records are grouped by task month ascending and date ascending. UUID string comparison breaks date ties. 2. Choose **Add project**. Enter a name and optional description, then Save. Duplicate names produce an inline error and retain entered values. 3. Choose **Add task**, or create a project from inside its editor. The project is automatically selected without losing other entered task data. A task needs an existing selected project, trimmed nonempty name, finite decimal cost, and real task date. Decimal comma input is accepted; negative costs, future dates, and sent dates before work dates are not prohibited. 4. Dates can be typed as `YYYY-MM-DD` or selected using native calendar controls. Today is the local calendar date; date-only strings are never converted via UTC instants. Optional description is trimmed and blank sent date means Not sent. Default create cost is 10. 5. Tap a task for every field and **Edit task**. Edits use the same prefilled form. Back prompts before discarding changed task/project inputs. Saves are disabled while in flight; only confirmed responses close/reset a form. 6. In details, **Mark as sent** asks for a date (today by default). **Mark as not sent** confirms clearing the date. Both explain that no email, invoice, notification, or message is transmitted. Each shortcut fetches the latest task, then sends a full writable record with only `sentOn` changed. 7. **History** contains **all tasks**, both statuses, by task date descending, with descending UUID strings breaking ties. Sent-on-create records appear here, not in Not sent. Missing historical projects have a fallback label and remain in totals; select a valid project before saving such records. 8. Pull down or choose Refresh to reconcile with the web client. Returning from the background also refreshes. Failed loads identify tasks/projects separately. Loaded data remains visible with an explicit stale warning. 9. After an uncertain write, the form stays open and Save is blocked. Review refreshed server records before explicitly allowing another save. If the record already exists/changed as intended, leave the form instead. No POST or stale PUT is automatically replayed. A deleted task is never recreated.
## Implementation map
| File | Responsibility | | --- | --- | | `data/model/Task.kt` | Response/request DTOs, exact decimal totals, validation, stable ordering, date-only helpers | | `data/remote/TasksApi.kt` | Plain-array task/project endpoints and full PUT contracts | | `data/repository/TasksRepository.kt` | Configured HTTPS origin, bearer header, timeouts, disabled automatic retries/redirects, sanitized text/JSON failures | | `ui/viewmodels/TasksViewModel.kt` | Concurrent list fetches, obsolete-response guards, forms, confirmed mutations and reconciliation | | `ui/screens/TasksScreen.kt` | Overview, details, task/project forms, clearable calendars, confirmation and error/review UI | | `res/values/tasks.xml` | English resource strings ready for translation; follows the existing English UI | | `MainNavigation.kt`, `ui/screens/AccountScreen.kt` | Section navigation, account settings, sign-out and reauthentication routing | | `data/local/TokenCipher.kt`, `SettingsManager.kt` | Secure token storage and legacy migration |
Paths above are relative to the application's package under `app/src/main`, except resources. Writable payloads contain `projectId`, `name`, numeric `cost`, `date`, `sentOn`, and `description`; never `id`, `projectName`, or `status`. Optional clears are explicit empty strings. HTTP errors expose only recognized validation messages through local resource strings, never raw server internals.
## Automated checks
Run from the repository root in PowerShell:
```powershell .\gradlew.bat :app:testDebugUnitTest :app:lintDebug :app:assembleDebug :app:assembleDebugAndroidTest --console=plain ```
With an Android device/emulator connected:
```powershell .\gradlew.bat :app:connectedDebugAndroidTest --console=plain ```
The Android test configuration now imports the Compose BOM, resolving the pre-existing missing version for `ui-test-junit4`. Core library desugaring supports `java.time` on the existing minimum SDK 24. Added dependencies were checked for known CVEs; none were reported at implementation time.
### Results on this workstation
- Debug application compilation and APK assembly: **passed**. - Android lint: **passed**, with non-blocking dependency/resource warnings. - JVM unit tests: **19 passed**, including 18 new Tasks tests and the existing example test. - Instrumentation test APK compilation: **passed**. - Android 15/API 35 Pixel 7 emulator: initial four Tasks UI tests plus the existing instrumentation example **passed** at default size/text settings. - Final instrumentation suite at 720×1280 pixels / density 360 (320dp width), 150% text, `Pacific/Kiritimati` (UTC+14): **6 passed**, including five Tasks tests and the existing example. This run also passed unit tests, lint, and debug APK assembly in the same Gradle invocation. - The five final Tasks UI tests rerun at 320dp width, **200% text**, and `America/Los_Angeles` (west of UTC): **5 passed**. Form tests exercised keyboard-open scrolling and decimal-comma/date-only text input. - A first small-screen run exposed an overview layout/testing issue; controls, summaries, and notices now scroll with the content instead of reserving a large fixed header, and tests explicitly scroll to cards. The final reruns above passed after that change. - Emulator execution used an isolated read-only, no-snapshot instance. No physical device, minimum-SDK emulator, or TalkBack validation was performed. - Live backend/web interoperability: **not performed**; deployment origins, test access, and representative shared records have not been supplied.
Unit coverage includes status derivation (absent/null/empty sent date), exact summary arithmetic including unassigned tasks, mixed History, UUID ties, decimal-comma numeric JSON, explicit optional clearing, required fields, leap/invalid dates and time zones on both sides of UTC, concurrent loads, obsolete responses, duplicate taps, retained forms, uncertain outcomes, session expiry, legacy project repair, and status updates based on current records. Retrofit fixtures cover 200/201, empty arrays, 400/401/403/404/409/500, plain-text and JSON errors, and simulated connectivity failures.
`TasksScreenTest` adds five backend-independent Compose tests for default pending/mixed History, status confirmation and preserved fields, project creation preserving task input, discard confirmation, and decimal-comma costs with date-only edits (including negative costs and sent dates before work dates).
Reports and APKs:
- `app/build/reports/tests/testDebugUnitTest/index.html` - `app/build/reports/lint-results-debug.html` - `app/build/reports/androidTests/connected/debug/index.html` (after execution) - `app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk` - `app/build/outputs/apk/androidTest/debug/app-debug-androidTest.apk`
## Remaining release QA and limitations
- Complete AC01–AC19 against the deployment and web client with shared records. Optional AC20/AC21 do not apply: Prepare, mark-all, reassignment, deletion, and project editing are intentionally omitted. - Validate supported OS versions (especially SDK 24), small screens, keyboard open, large fonts/TalkBack, long names/descriptions, decimal-comma input, calendar rotation, time zones on both sides of UTC, and returning from background while requests are pending. Capture screenshots or recordings of the walkthrough using authorized non-sensitive test data. The automated small-screen/large-text/timezone subset above is complete on API 35; the broader release matrix and manual screen-reader/calendar checks remain open. - Exercise slow/failed connections, expired sessions, duplicate project names, deletion by another client, and a timed-out create that actually succeeded. Confirm retained input, stale labels, explicit reconciliation, and no duplicates. - The backend has no ETags/version checks. Fetch-before-status-update narrows but **does not eliminate** the full-record overwrite race. Ordinary edits can overwrite another client's changes. This is not conflict-safe editing. - Drafts survive configuration changes in the ViewModel, not process death. There is no offline write queue, background polling, or disk task cache. - No production signing/release artifact was generated or altered. Existing signing keys, credentials, and unrelated working-tree artifacts are untouched.

# Android Tasks section
Implemented against the Spending Tracker task/project contract prepared 9 November 2026 and updated 10 November 2026. This repository is a native Android application (Jetpack Compose, Hilt, Retrofit/Gson), not the web/backend repository referenced by the handoff. No backend changes or iOS target are included.
## Integration clarifications
- The web homepage/route policy does not change mobile's global start screen: mobile continues to open Notes after login. Tasks remains available to every authenticated role, matching the API's authentication-only policy. - Work Tasks uses UUIDs, projects, costs, work dates and `sentOn`. It is separate from the numeric-ID **Tasks list** folder type in [Notes & lists](NOTES_AND_LISTS.md), which uses `completed` and optional `endDate`. Work-task PUTs replace the full writable record; Notes PUTs preserve omitted fields. - There are no task reminders, Telegram schedules or message-delivery actions. Marking as sent only stores a date. Records are shared among authenticated users. - Required first-release operations only: no Prepare, mark-all, reassignment, task/project deletion or project editing was added.
## Setup
1. Use the existing Android Studio/Gradle wrapper setup and installed SDKs specified by `app/build.gradle.kts` and `gradle/libs.versions.toml`. 2. Obtain the development/staging/production **HTTPS origin** and a test account from the deployment owner through the normal secure channel. No origin or credentials are embedded in this feature. Use an origin such as `https://your-deployment.example/`, not a device-local `localhost`, and use valid certificates. Do not disable certificate checks. 3. Configure that origin in the existing login screen and sign in normally. Prefer the origin root (without `/api`) for compatibility with the existing Notes/login client. Tasks always addresses `/api/tasks` and `/api/projects` at the origin root, so it never produces `/api/api/...`. 4. Open **Tasks** from the bottom navigation. All authenticated roles use the same actions; task/project data is **shared**, not user-private. **Account** contains the workspace connection, biometric preference, and confirmed sign-out. Bottom navigation is hidden in task details/editors so leaving unsaved edits goes through the normal Back/discard flow.
Bearer tokens reuse the existing session and are now encrypted at rest using a non-exportable Android Keystore AES-GCM key. Existing plaintext stored tokens are migrated on first read. A restored/corrupted encrypted token without its key is invalidated and requires login. Task data is only held in the navigation-entry ViewModel, not persisted as an offline cache. A Tasks 401 clears the session, biometric session flag, Tasks state, and protected navigation stack. There is no refresh-token endpoint or retry loop.
## Walkthrough
1. Open Tasks: **Not sent** is the initial view. Check pending count, pending EUR total, and total task count. Pending records are grouped by task month ascending and date ascending. UUID string comparison breaks date ties. 2. Choose **Add project**. Enter a name and optional description, then Save. Duplicate names produce an inline error and retain entered values. 3. Choose **Add task**, or create a project from inside its editor. The project is automatically selected without losing other entered task data. A task needs an existing selected project, trimmed nonempty name, finite decimal cost, and real task date. Decimal comma input is accepted; negative costs, future dates, and sent dates before work dates are not prohibited. 4. Dates can be typed as `YYYY-MM-DD` or selected using native calendar controls. Today is the local calendar date; date-only strings are never converted via UTC instants. Optional description is trimmed and blank sent date means Not sent. Default create cost is 10. 5. Tap a task for every field and **Edit task**. Edits use the same prefilled form. Back prompts before discarding changed task/project inputs. Saves are disabled while in flight; only confirmed responses close/reset a form. 6. In details, **Mark as sent** asks for a date (today by default). **Mark as not sent** confirms clearing the date. Both explain that no email, invoice, notification, or message is transmitted. Each shortcut fetches the latest task, then sends a full writable record with only `sentOn` changed. 7. **History** contains **all tasks**, both statuses, by task date descending, with descending UUID strings breaking ties. Sent-on-create records appear here, not in Not sent. Missing historical projects have a fallback label and remain in totals; select a valid project before saving such records. 8. Pull down or choose Refresh to reconcile with the web client. Returning from the background also refreshes. Failed loads identify tasks/projects separately. Loaded data remains visible with an explicit stale warning. 9. After an uncertain write, the form stays open and Save is blocked. Review refreshed server records before explicitly allowing another save. If the record already exists/changed as intended, leave the form instead. No POST or stale PUT is automatically replayed. A deleted task is never recreated. Closing/reopening editors does not bypass this guard. Review is only accepted once both datasets have loaded successfully and no refresh is in flight. Response-parsing failures during writes are treated as uncertain, not as safe local configuration errors: the server may already have stored the change.
## Implementation map
| File | Responsibility | | --- | --- | | `data/model/Task.kt` | Response/request DTOs, exact decimal totals, validation, stable ordering, date-only helpers | | `data/remote/TasksApi.kt` | Plain-array task/project endpoints and full PUT contracts | | `data/repository/TasksRepository.kt` | Configured HTTPS origin, bearer header, timeouts, disabled automatic retries/redirects, sanitized text/JSON failures | | `ui/viewmodels/TasksViewModel.kt` | Concurrent list fetches, obsolete-response guards, forms, confirmed mutations and reconciliation | | `ui/screens/TasksScreen.kt` | Overview, details, task/project forms, clearable calendars, confirmation and error/review UI | | `res/values/tasks.xml` | English resource strings ready for translation; follows the existing English UI | | `MainNavigation.kt`, `ui/screens/AccountScreen.kt` | Section navigation, account settings, sign-out and reauthentication routing | | `data/local/TokenCipher.kt`, `SettingsManager.kt` | Secure token storage and legacy migration | | `app/src/test/.../TasksContractTest.kt` | HTTP fixtures, numeric payloads, optional clears, dates, validation, status, totals and ordering | | `app/src/test/.../TasksControllerTest.kt` | Concurrent/stale loads, obsolete responses, forms, status preservation, duplicate saves, authentication and uncertain outcomes | | `app/src/androidTest/.../TasksScreenTest.kt` | Compose workflows, large-text/dark mode and fixture screenshots |
Paths above are relative to the application's package under `app/src/main`, except resources and test paths beginning with `app/`. Writable payloads contain `projectId`, `name`, numeric `cost`, `date`, `sentOn`, and `description`; never `id`, `projectName`, or `status`. Optional clears are explicit empty strings. HTTP errors expose only recognized validation messages through local resource strings, never raw server internals.
## Build and automated checks
Run from the repository root in PowerShell:
```powershell .\gradlew.bat :app:testDebugUnitTest :app:lintDebug :app:assembleDebug --console=plain ```
Run the Tasks screen suite on a chosen emulator (set `ANDROID_SERIAL` so an attached physical device is not selected inadvertently):
```powershell $env:ANDROID_SERIAL = 'emulator-5554' .\gradlew.bat :app:connectedDebugAndroidTest '-Pandroid.testInstrumentationRunnerArguments.class=com.elialombardi.piccistodo.TasksScreenTest' --console=plain ```
Some connected-test runners reset display overrides and uninstall the test APK afterward. For a specific size, build both APKs with `:app:assembleDebug` and `:app:assembleDebugAndroidTest`, then install/reinstall them before a direct run:
```powershell adb -s emulator-5554 install -r -t app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk adb -s emulator-5554 install -r -t app/build/outputs/apk/androidTest/debug/app-debug-androidTest.apk adb -s emulator-5554 shell wm size 720x1280 adb -s emulator-5554 shell wm density 320 adb -s emulator-5554 shell am instrument -w -r -e class com.elialombardi.piccistodo.TasksScreenTest com.elialombardi.piccistodo.test/androidx.test.runner.AndroidJUnitRunner adb -s emulator-5554 shell wm size reset adb -s emulator-5554 shell wm density reset ```
Record `wm size`/`wm density` in the run log and restore both even if a run fails. The test captures synthetic-data screenshots under the app's external-files `tasks-qa` directory. No staging access or embedded credentials are used.
Core library desugaring supports `java.time` on minimum SDK 24.
### Local validation, 10 November 2026
- Debug build and lint passed. Lint: **0 errors, 38 warnings, 2 hints**; these warnings/hints remain and are not represented as a clean warning-free release. - **66 JVM tests passed**, including **25 Tasks tests** (9 contract, 16 controller). - **All 6 Tasks screen tests passed on each of three API 35 emulator profiles:**
| Profile | Verified display | Result | Log under `app/build/` | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Default phone | 1080×2400 px, 420 dpi | 6 passed, 0 failures | `tasks-phone-validation.txt` | | Small phone | 720×1280 px, 320 dpi (360×640 dp) | 6 passed, 0 failures | `tasks-small-phone-validation.txt` | | Tablet-size override | 1600×2560 px, 240 dpi (about 1067×1707 dp) | 6 passed, 0 failures | `tasks-tablet-validation.txt` |
Small-phone/tablet runs invoked instrumentation directly after verifying the display overrides; the display was restored afterward. These are size profiles on the same emulator, not separate hardware-device or OS-version certifications. The screen suite exercises mixed-status History, status confirmation/clearing, project creation while retaining task input, decimal-comma input with the keyboard open, disabled Save without projects, discard confirmation, stale loads, retained uncertain edits, and 1.8× text in dark mode. - HTTP fixtures exercise 200/201 responses, empty arrays, 400/401/403/404/409/500 errors, plain-text and JSON error parsing, and full numeric PUT/POST payloads. Controller fixtures simulate connectivity failures, lost create responses, stale refreshes, concurrent edits/deletions and expired authentication. - Date-only JVM checks cover Kiritimati (UTC+14), Los Angeles (west of UTC), and Tokyo; decimal-comma input, negative costs and unconstrained date order are covered. - These are **local fixture checks**, not proof of staging/backend integration, mobile/web persistence, production HTTPS configuration or device accessibility.
### Acceptance coverage map
| Handoff scenarios | Local evidence | Still needs deployment/device QA | | --- | --- | --- | | AC01–AC03, AC11–AC12, AC14 | Summary/status/order/legacy contract tests; loading/empty/controller tests | Representative shared records and role accounts | | AC04–AC08, AC13 | Project-selection preservation, numeric payloads, full edits, validation/date tests | Reload in both mobile and web; real duplicate-name behavior | | AC09–AC10 | Fresh-fetch/full-record status tests; date clearing and preservation | Concurrent real-client edits and server persistence | | AC15–AC19 | Stale retention, obsolete-response guards, 401/403/404, input retention, duplicate-save and uncertain-outcome tests | Real slow/offline networks, expired sessions, process/device behavior | | AC20–AC21 | Not applicable | Optional operations intentionally omitted |

## Remaining release QA and limitations
- Obtain reachable environment origins and test accounts through the normal secure channel, then complete AC01–AC19 against the deployment and web client with shared records. No live backend validation is claimed by this delivery. Optional AC20/AC21 do not apply: Prepare, mark-all, reassignment, deletion, and project editing are intentionally omitted. - Validate supported OS versions (especially SDK 24), small screens, keyboard open, large fonts/TalkBack, long names/descriptions, decimal-comma input, calendar rotation, time zones on both sides of UTC, and returning from background while requests are pending. Capture screenshots or recordings of the walkthrough using authorized non-sensitive test data. Perform this validation manually in addition to the automated fixture checks. API 24 and the full supported OS matrix, physical-device TalkBack/focus/touch targets, native date-picker/time-zone behavior, and translated-label review remain release checks. Automated screenshots do not constitute visual or accessibility sign-off. - Exercise slow/failed connections, expired sessions, duplicate project names, deletion by another client, and a timed-out create that actually succeeded. Confirm retained input, stale labels, explicit reconciliation, and no duplicates. - The backend has no ETags/version checks. Fetch-before-status-update narrows but **does not eliminate** the full-record overwrite race. Ordinary edits can overwrite another client's changes. This is not conflict-safe editing. - Drafts survive configuration changes in the ViewModel, not process death. There is no offline write queue, background polling, or disk task cache. - No production signing/release artifact was generated or altered. Existing signing keys, credentials, and unrelated working-tree artifacts are untouched.
